title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page ends a letter (archive cote dated 1965) that sketches a p-adic analogue of the comparison between Betti/ℓ-adic cohomology and de Rham cohomology.

(1) Setting, carried over from the previous page. K is algebraically closed and complete for a non-archimedean valuation, of characteristic 0, with residue characteristic p. X is a (proper smooth) K-variety. Grothendieck hopes for a natural Z_p-linear map H^*(X_et, Z_p) → H^*_dR(X/K) inducing an isomorphism H^*(X,Z_p) ⊗ K ≅ H^*_dR(X).

(2) Proposed route. Pass to Tate's rigid-analytic space X^an, viewed as a site (a G-topology), not a topological space. Torsion étale cohomology should agree with X^an cohomology. Optimistically, H^*(X^an, Z_p) would be the projective limit of H^*(X^an, Z/p^n), hence equal to H^*_et(X, Z_p). Then Z_p ⊂ K ⊂ O_{X^an} gives H^*(X^an, Z_p) → H^*(X^an, K) → H^*_dR(X^an), and rigid GAGA gives H^*_dR(X^an) = H^*_dR(X).

(3) What this page adds. The missing input is a 'rigid-analytic Poincaré lemma': on X^an, the de Rham complex should resolve the sheaf of locally constant K-valued functions.
- Grothendieck notes this is trivial in naive p-adic analytic geometry (convergent power series on small polydiscs).
- He notes it is delicate for the much coarser rigid (admissible) topology. Indeed, on a closed affinoid disc, integrating Σ a_n x^n dx produces coefficients a_n/(n+1), which may not tend to 0. Covers by smaller discs are not admissible, so the lemma fails.
- He doubts that rigid cohomology with constant coefficients gives the right Betti numbers. He recalls Tate saying this already fails for H^1 of elliptic curves: one gets more than étale cohomology would give, but not the whole cohomology. That matches the modern picture: for a Tate curve G_m/q^Z the topological H^1 has rank 1 (the skeleton is a circle), and rank 0 for good reduction.
- He still expects the rigid topology to play a role.

(4) Characteristic p, a 'worn-out' remark. There is a map H^*(X, F_p) → H^*_dR(X), obtained as follows.
- Compute de Rham cohomology in the étale topology; this is legitimate because the Ω^i are quasi-coherent.
- Use the second hypercohomology spectral sequence H^p(X, H^q(Ω^•)) ⇒ H^*_dR(X), now called the conjugate spectral sequence.
- The map factors as H^*(X, F_p) → H^*(X, O_X) (Artin–Schreier) followed by H^*(O_X) → H^*_dR. The second arrow comes from O_X ≅ H^0(Ω^•) via f ↦ f^p, the degree-0 Cartier isomorphism.
- The composite H^n(O_X) → H^n_dR → H^n(O_X), with the last arrow the edge map of the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence, 'can hardly be anything but Frobenius'. It is Frobenius, since Z^0 = O_X^p ⊂ O_X.
- He concludes that only the 'true' p-adic cohomology will yield new results.
errors: The hoped-for natural K-linear (or Z_p-linear) map H^*_et(X, Z_p) → H^*_dR(X/K) giving H_et ⊗ K ≅ H_dR cannot exist canonically. For G_m it would require a p-adic period '2πi' in C_p, which Tate showed does not exist. The correct statement needs Fontaine's B_dR. Grothendieck's stated doubts are justified.

The rigid Poincaré lemma for the constant sheaf K is false on affinoids, because of p-adic denominators in integration. So rigid cohomology with constant coefficients does not compute de Rham cohomology. Grothendieck suspects this and attributes a counterexample to Tate.

Minor: the sheaves H^q(Ω^•) are naturally quasi-coherent on the Frobenius twist X^(p) rather than on X. The isomorphism O_X ≅ H^0(Ω^•) via f ↦ f^p is p-linear (it needs a perfect base field). This is harmless for the argument.

ideas.what: Conjectural natural comparison H^*(X, Z_p) ⊗ K ≅ H^*_dR(X) for varieties over complete algebraically closed p-adic fields
ideas.modern_name: p-adic de Rham comparison theorem (C_dR); Grothendieck's 'mysterious functor'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (problem, ICM 1970); Fontaine (B_dR, 1982); Faltings, Tsuji, Scholze (proofs)
ideas.where_published: 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux', ICM Nice 1970 (mysterious functor). The 1965 rigid-analytic formulation: unsure

ideas.what: Use Tate's rigid-analytic site X^an, compare torsion étale cohomology with X^an cohomology, and get Z_p-coefficients by projective limits
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of étale cohomology of rigid spaces with algebraic étale cohomology (Huber, Berkovich); pro-étale site (Bhatt–Scholze, Scholze)

ideas.what: Rigid-analytic Poincaré lemma as the key input, plus doubt that it holds for constant coefficients in the coarse rigid topology
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré lemma for period sheaves (OB_dR) on the pro-étale site; failure of the naive Poincaré lemma on affinoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Scholze, 'p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties' (2013), for the correct version with period sheaves

ideas.what: Tate's remark that constant-coefficient rigid cohomology gives too small an H^1 for elliptic curves
ideas.modern_name: Topological/Berkovich cohomology of the analytification (rank 1 for a Tate curve via its skeleton)

ideas.what: Characteristic p: H^*(X, F_p) → H^*(O_X) → H^*_dR via Artin–Schreier and Cartier (f ↦ f^p), using the conjugate spectral sequence; the composite H(O) → H_dR → H(O) is Frobenius
ideas.modern_name: Conjugate spectral sequence and Cartier isomorphism in degree 0; Artin–Schreier map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre 1958 (Artin–Schreier and Frobenius on H(O)); Cartier; Katz (conjugate spectral sequence, 1970)

missed.claim: Around 1965 Grothendieck proposed attacking the p-adic étale/de Rham comparison through the cohomology of the rigid-analytic site. He identified a 'rigid Poincaré lemma' (de Rham complex resolving constants) as the crux, and saw why it should fail for constant coefficients. This is structurally the route Scholze took in 2013: replace the constant sheaf with the period sheaf B_dR^+ on the pro-étale site of the rigid space, where the Poincaré lemma for OB_dR holds.
missed.quote: un "lemme de Poincaré" rigide-analytique, disant que sur X^an, le complexe de De-Rham est bien une résolution du faisceau des fonctions constantes ... Il reste plausible néanmoins ... que la topologie rigide-analytique aura son rôle à jouer dans ces questions.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is historical evidence that the rigid-analytic/Poincaré-lemma strategy for p-adic comparison was envisaged by Grothendieck years before the 'mysterious functor' (1970). That pre-history is not usually cited in accounts of p-adic Hodge theory.

missed.claim: Grothendieck records an otherwise undocumented remark of Tate. Constant-coefficient rigid cohomology of an elliptic curve gives more than (torsion) étale-type information but less than full H^1. This is an early observation of what Berkovich skeleton cohomology later made precise.
missed.quote: Tate m'avait dit que c'était déjà faux pour le H^1 des courbes elliptiques ... on trouverait un peu plus que pour la cohomologie étale, mais quand même pas toute la cohomologie.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor historical attribution to Tate concerning the topology of analytifications of Tate curves.

deep.surprise_reason: Grothendieck's general p-adic comparison problem (the mysterious functor) is well known. Less known is this explicit mid-1960s plan via the rigid site and a rigid Poincaré lemma, together with the correct diagnosis of why constant coefficients fail and the recorded remark of Tate. It foreshadows the period-sheaf approach of Scholze. The characteristic-p part is, in his own words, 'éculé'.

'beaucoup' appears in the typescript as the overstruck 'beamucoup'.
